question: Do the currently adopted parameters let the paper's mainstream claim run end to end?
answer: NO.  Links (1)-(4) run; link (5) -- the claim itself -- does not.
the_claim: Same operators, same resolution, same representative points, one input different: chiral only -> P1 has no rho (Fig.7);  + UV -> P1 acquires a rho (Fig.9).  TASK_SDP_AUDIT_AND_CLOSE_ZH.md section 0.

blockers.what: link (5) certifies under NO adopted setting
blockers.note: The uncertified values 0.51-0.94 are relaxation upper bounds, an order of magnitude above the paper's ~0.08; they are not results.  Root cause is the ~1e35 conditioning, the same one that kills every high-disk-count solve.
blockers.owner: engineering (SDPB on the full disk set) + physics Q1/Q4

blockers.what: the rho criterion is not usable as implemented
blockers.evidence: On a chiral-only CERTIFIED point -- where the paper says there is no rho -- crossing_90_GeV returns 1.497 GeV, while delta_11(0.77 GeV) = 19.8 deg and min eta = 0.9997 (fully elastic).  crossing_90 alone reports a rho where there is none.
blockers.note: Even a certified link (5) could not settle the contrast without a real criterion.
The contrast is defined at tip / ref / mid; the driver must be extended.

inconsistencies.what: m_q default is the arithmetic mean 5.650 MeV
inconsistencies.evidence: (2.56) is reproduced to 0.7% only by the rms 5.886 MeV (arithmetic gives 9.3%).  (3.75) bounds |F|^2 by 2 m_q^2 eps_FF, so the adopted default makes that bound 7.9% TIGHTER than the paper's own moments imply.
inconsistencies.tested: does NOT change link (5)'s feasibility, but it does bias the final numbers
